items.title: Albert Morgan Interview, 1958-08-19
items.q: first job I had was with my brother, Isaiah. Oh, yeah. He brought me up with his little band.

ctx.x: When you started, were you bowing mostly or picking?

Well, mostly bowing. Because he wanted me to start to, see, that's, that's the, you get the sound on the bass better, like that, see, when you're bowing. So, so I, I did pretty good during the Lent months and, and when the season did open up that Easter, first job I had was with my brother, Isaiah. Oh, yeah. He brought me up with his little band. Just, just that, that one job, you know. I, I played with him. He had a little gig, we call them nowadays. So, one of those picnics. Oh, yeah. On the, on the, on the,…
The time you got on the boat where you, most of the people picked you up at the time?

items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: My brother Al was playing with them.

ctx.x: Trombone was, uh, Yankee. And his, uh, they only had six pieces. But they didn't make no recording until I take him with us. See, they was trying to, seems like they were trying to double cross him after he got sick, figured he couldn't play anymore. And trying to put Willie Pajot in his place when they went to Mobile. They went down there and they made a failure. So, the man came and told him, says, uh, that wasn't Sam Morgan Band. What do you heard? So, I told him, I said, we'll take you with us. Oh, he didn't…
Which hall was this that was with them? The Blar and Ed Blar Hall?
